Markus / team —

Draft commercial proposal below (working copy). I attached a redline for the SOW & an example ramp schedule (proposed_ramp_schedule.xlsx).

Proposal (commercial):
- Pilot term: 6 months.
- Opt-out: Customer may terminate the pilot with 60 days' written notice any time during the first 6 months.
- Downsizing protection: Instead of a full termination charge, customer may downscale committed capacity once during the first 90 days after opt-out notice takes effect; revenue protection is applied as a staircase: 70% of original committed monthly fee for first 30 days after downsize, 50% for days 31–60, 30% for days 61–90, then full move to new tier.
- Minimums: Applies only to pilots <= $350,000 ARR and only if customer has signed our standard data protection addendum (SOC2 or equivalent).
- Tradeoffs for Redwood: If we accept, request a 10% increase in monthly fees for the pilot (one-time uplift) to offset churn risk or require prepayment for first 2 months.

Why this works: gives NovaMed runway to test without killing deal economics. Limits our downside with a time-bound staircase and a size cap.

I'll propose exact contract language in the redline (attached). Karthik — please review for legal exposure; I underlined the concession points in the PDF.

- Marissa
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Thanks team. I reviewed Marissa's redline and flagged three legal points:

1) Ambiguity around "downscale once" — we should limit to a single downscale event per pilot term and require written acknowledgement of the target post-downscale tier.
2) Revenue protection staircase needs precise math example and a hard cap on total credits to avoid open-ended liability. Suggest cap = 3 months of staircased protection or 25% of total pilot value, whichever is less.
3) Data/security precondition: require SOC2 Type II attestation or signed security questionnaire; if not present, concession not permitted.

Suggested executive approval ask: allow Deal Desk to accept the concession (60-day opt-out + 90-day staircase) for pilots <= $350k ARR provided Finance applies an upfront 2-month prepayment or a 10% uplift; additionally, cap Redwood's exposure at 25% of pilot value.

I've added redline comments in NovaMed_redline_v1.pdf. Laura — will you confirm the accounting/crediting approach and whether the cap creates any revenue recognition headaches?

- Karthik
Staff Counsel, Redwood Inference

All — quick finance take: the cap (25% of pilot value) is preferred over an open-ended staircase from an accounting standpoint. Two technical notes:

- If we require 2 months' prepayment, revenue will be recognized monthly as services are delivered; we should avoid large refundable balances. Recommend the prepayment be non-refundable and applied to the final months after any downscale adjustments.
- If we accept a 10% uplift instead of prepayment, ensure the uplift is contractually non-refundable and documented as a price premium — that avoids tricky refund accounting.

Otherwise I'm OK with the ask for pilots <= $350k ARR.

- Laura
Director, Finance Operations, Redwood Inference
